title: Inspection & Sign-Off Report
source: spec/Inspection_Signoff_Report.html — UNLIKE every other template in this library, this one has NO paper original. It is a self-authored generic inspection report, not a consultant-accepted form, so the repo's usual verification ("print the source to PDF and the app's output to PDF and compare page by page", CLAUDE.md) has nothing external to compare against: the source is a scrolling web page with no A4 geometry at all. What is pinned instead is the sheet's CONTENT — its eight sections, their fields and their wording — and the parity test asserts that. Layout is this library's own, not a reproduction. The file arrived blank (no record values to strip).

sections.title: Inspector Details
sections._note:
Section 2 of the source, carried whole. The section numbering starts at 2 because the source's section 1 (Report Information) is the record header — the library's standing idiom for a document band directly under the title (`fire-alarm-test.json`, `meter-verification-record.json`).

**One field of section 1 is deliberately NOT carried: `Report Status` (Draft / Under Review / Final / Rejected).** This app already owns record status — `draft → completed → submitted_for_witness → witnessed → accepted / rejected` (SPEC §6) — and prints it in every page footer (§7). A second status the user sets by hand would sit on the same signed page as the app's and disagree with it: someone selects "Final" on a record the app still holds at `draft`, and the printed document says both. Same call `staircase-pressurization.json` makes about the source's own Form No. / Rev., for the same reason — "a second pair of revision numbers on the same page invites the two to disagree". To restore it anyway, add to the header fields:
`{ "id": "report_status", "label": "Report Status", "type": "dropdown", "options": ["Draft", "Under Review", "Final", "Rejected"] }`

Inspector Name / Company overlap the Inspector signature slot below, which captures a name, a company and a signed date of its own. Both are kept, because the source keeps both and because they answer different questions: this block is who was assigned, the slot is who actually signed. Title / Role, Employee ID and Contact have no equivalent in a signature slot at all.

Inspection Type is a `dropdown` over the source's own seven options, in the source's order.

sections.title: Scope & References
sections._note: Section 3, both boxes verbatim. The source's placeholder text ("e.g. ISO 9001, ASTM A123, Drawing Rev. C…") is a hint, not template wording, and is not carried — a placeholder that printed would read as content.

sections.title: Inspection Checklist
sections._note:
Section 4. The source's Pass / Fail / N/A radio pills are the `pass_fail_na` field type — the library's existing three-state control, so a Fail is derivable as an outstanding item (SPEC §6) without declaring bespoke `status` states.

**`min_rows` is 3, against the source's `DEFAULT_ROWS = 8`.** The source seeds eight blank rows because a web page can afford them; a printed sheet cannot, and a four-item inspection would print four filled rows and four empty ones. The engineer adds what the inspection needs — the same trim every other converted table in this library makes (`fire-alarm-test.json`, `pa-system-test.json`), and what replaces the source's "+ Add Item" button.

Widths are set for a portrait sheet, where the print body is 688px and a table is not shrunk to fit: four columns of ordinary wording is comfortably inside the ~6-column ceiling, and Findings takes the largest share because it carries the longest text. The `#` column is `auto_number`, matching the source's own first column.

sections.title: Defects & Non-Conformances
sections._note: Section 5, both boxes. Free text, as the source has them — this template does not tabulate defects into rows with owners and due dates, because the source does not, and inventing a structure here would be a form the user did not send.

sections.title: Overall Inspection Result
sections._note:
Section 6. The source offers PASS / FAIL only here — no N/A, unlike the per-item checklist above — so this is a two-state `status` row rather than another `pass_fail_na`. That asymmetry is the source's and is kept.

The source's separate "Overall Comments & Recommendations" box is this row's `remarks` textarea, so the verdict and the comment on it stay one thing rather than drifting into two blocks that can contradict each other.

sections.title: Supporting Documents & Attachments

fields.label: List of Attachments (photos, test reports, drawings, etc.)

sections._note:
Section 7 — a TYPED LIST of what is attached, which is all the source is.

It is not the app's photo feature and does not replace it: real photos attach to the record and print as A4 photo appendix pages behind it via the print-step "Include photo attachment pages" toggle (SPEC §12), which stores them as evidence that syncs and locks with the record. This box is the index a reader sees on the report page; the toggle is where the photos themselves live.

sections.title: Sign-Off
sections._note:
Section 8's three pads, in the source's order. The source pairs each pad with a printed-name box and a date box; a `signature` slot captures name, company and signed date itself, so those boxes are the slot and are not declared as extra fields.

**Stage mapping — the three pads land on the three gated steps of the workflow (SPEC §6), one each:**
- Inspector → `contractor`, gating draft → completed. Required: the report is not issued unsigned.
- Supervisor / Reviewer → `witness`, gating submitted_for_witness → witnessed. A supervisor's review IS the witness step in this app; `check` was the alternative and is rejected here because no workflow rule references that stage, so the signature would print without gating anything.
- Client / Witness → `client`, gating witnessed → accepted, the final acceptance.

The third pad's label merges two words this app keeps apart. It is mapped to `client` rather than `witness` because it is the LAST signature on the sheet, and the last signature is the one that should close the record — mapping it to `witness` would leave acceptance ungated by any signature at all.

Only the Inspector is `required`, following `sanitary-pipe-flood-test.json`: a report may legitimately be issued before the reviewer and the client have got to it. Note that `required` is declarative on a signature — `satisfiedStages` gates on the STAGE regardless of it, so an unsigned optional slot still holds its own transition.
